title: PowerPoint: edit presentations with Copilot in the DoD cloud
summary: Hold for corrections to the licensing controls. Removing the paid Copilot licence does not remove all Copilot access, and the Assign licenses panel is not the documented route for unassigning a licence. The roadmap facts and the warning about conflicting DoD availability documentation are supported.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Roles; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: At least License Administrator or User Administrator is required to assign licences.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The licence assignment path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. ... Select a product. ... On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId <user> -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigning or removing the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence governs Copilot access as a whole.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel).
claims.fix: Replace 'Governs Copilot access as a whole, not this capability separately' and equivalent prose with 'Governs access to the licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) features, not this capability separately; removing the add-on does not remove all Basic Copilot access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-overview alongside the service description.

claims.claim: The roadmap description announces no change to sign-in or permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint helps you create, edit, and refine presentations through natural language—right inside your deck. ... Available to Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) users.

claims.claim: A prompt can make presentation-wide design changes and edit content across multiple slides.
claims.quote: Ask it to reformat your presentation to match the branded template style, applying consistent colors, fonts, and layouts throughout ... "Update slides 4-6 for a UK audience."
claims.fix: Cite https://support.microsoft.com/topic/008f17aa-8e5f-4cda-ba6c-0588000bdad7 for the multi-slide editing statement, and phrase it as general PowerPoint behaviour rather than confirmed DoD availability: 'The PowerPoint support page describes presentation-wide restyling and edits across several slides; confirm this behaviour in the DoD pilot.'

claims.claim: The government cloud overview says releases typically lag commercial environments.
claims.quote: Release timing typically lags behind commercial environments.

claims.claim: Brand kit prerequisites include separate mail-enabled security groups for brand managers and personal brand kit creators.
claims.quote: Create a separate mail-enabled security group for brand managers who can publish and manage official brand kits. ... Create a mail-enabled security group for users who can create and edit personal brand kits.

claims.claim: The brand kit governance page describes two independent policies.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot provides two independent policies for brand kit governance:

claims.claim: The Enterprise Brand Manager policy controls who can publish, edit and manage official brand kits.
claims.quote: Enterprise Brand Manager policy | Who can publish, edit, and manage official brand kits.

claims.claim: The Restrict brand kit creation policy controls who can create and edit personal brand kits.
claims.quote: Restrict brand kit creation policy | Who can create and edit personal brand kits.

claims.claim: Publishing a personal brand kit as an official kit requires satisfying both policy checks.
claims.quote: To publish a personal brand kit as an official brand kit, a user must satisfy both policy checks.

claims.claim: The documentation checked does not establish whether the brand kit prerequisites and policies apply in DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot brand kits government DoD availability governance policies'; 'brand kits DoD'. Read brand kit governance, service description and government overview. Governance covers brand kits generally without establishing their availability in DoD.

claims.claim: The Assign licenses panel can be used to assign or remove the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Unassign licenses by using the Licenses page ... Select a product. ... Select the check boxes of the users or groups for whom you want to unassign licenses. ... Select Unassign licenses.
claims.fix: Replace the rollout bullet with 'Assign the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for pilot users through Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses. To remove it, go to Billing > Licenses, select the product and the users or groups, then select Unassign licenses. Set-MgUserLicense can also assign or remove licences; a License Administrator or User Administrator can manage the assignments.' The cited assignment article documents these UI routes; the cited PowerShell article shows both operations.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense can also remove licences.
claims.quote:
# Unassign E3
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId "belindan@litwareinc.com" -AddLicenses @{} -RemoveLicenses @($e3Sku.SkuId)

claims.claim: Billing > Licenses is where administrators can list the users holding the Copilot add-on.
claims.quote: Group-based assignments If a license is assigned to a group, the group name appears in the list instead of individual users. To see which users are receiving the license through that group, go to the Teams & groups > Active teams & groups page to view its members.
claims.fix: Replace the inventory bullet with 'Review assignments in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Billing > Licenses, then select the Microsoft 365 Copilot product. For group-based assignments, inspect the group's members under Teams & groups > Active teams & groups to identify the users.'

claims.claim: The cited introductory Office editing support page describes consumer Microsoft 365 plans.
claims.quote: Editing with Copilot in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word is a way to create content within the Microsoft Copilot experience for Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, and Premium plans.

claims.claim: That consumer-oriented support page says editing in Office apps uses Anthropic models.
claims.quote: Editing with Copilot in your Office apps uses Anthropic models.

claims.claim: Learn says Claude models are not available to DoD customers.
claims.quote: Claude models aren't available for federal customers in GCC or for any customers in GCC High and Department of Defense (DoD) environments.
